newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae bought $2.1 bln of loans in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae bought $2.1 bln of loans in Q2.

text.p: Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) said Friday it bought $2.1 billion of student loans in the second quarter, compared with $2.4 billion a year earlier and $2.1 billion in the 1997 first quarter.

Sallie Mae said an additional $1.1 billion in purchases and future purchase commitments were postponed by sellers following statements by a group opposing management, the Committee to Restore Value (CRV), that it will begin origination of student loans if it gains control of the company.
Sallie Mae said the total portfolio of managed laons rose to $41.5 billion at June 30 from $37.4 billion a year earlier.
During the second quarter, the company securitized $2.5 billion of student loans, bringing the total of securitized loans outstanding to $10.0 billion.
More than 70 percent of second-quarter loan purchases came from lenders who have forward purchase commitments with Sallie Mae, about the same as in the first quarter and the year-earlier quarter.
Sallie Mae said the pipeline of loans currently serviced and committed for purchase by Sallie Mae was $3.5 billion on June 30, about the same as a year earlier.
